10001.text:
It was a bright and steady morning when the committee first gathered to
discuss the matter of fixtures. The room was small, the coffee was cold,
and nobody wished to be the first to speak.

Nevertheless the chairperson called the session to order and read the
minutes of the previous meeting aloud, pausing now and then to correct
a date or a name.

By afternoon the discussion had turned, as such discussions often do,
toward matters no one had planned to raise. The fixtures themselves sat
patiently in their crates, indifferent to the debate.

When at last a vote was called, the outcome surprised no one who had
been paying attention, and the meeting adjourned before the light
outside had fully faded.

10002.text:
The road out of the village ran straight for a while before it began to
bend gently along the line of the river, and the walker who had set out
that morning found no reason to hurry.

Fields opened on either side, some freshly turned, some still holding
the pale stubble of the last harvest, and a heron stood motionless in
the shallows as though it had always been there and always would.

By the time the sun stood directly overhead the walker had reached the
old stone bridge, where a peddler had set out a small collection of
buttons and thread on a folding table, and where, for a while, nothing
at all seemed to need doing.

The return journey took longer than the outward one, as return journeys
often do, and dusk had settled over the fields by the time the village
lights came back into view.

10003.text:
Il etait une fois, dans un petit village pres de la riviere, un
horloger qui ne reparait plus que des montres arretees. Chaque matin il
ouvrait son atelier avant le lever du soleil et attendait des clients
qui ne venaient presque jamais.

Un jour, une vieille femme entra et posa sur le comptoir une montre de
poche tres ancienne, sans un mot d'explication, puis elle repartit
aussitot sans attendre de reponse.

L'horloger ouvrit la montre avec precaution et decouvrit a l'interieur
un petit mot plie, ecrit d'une main tremblante, qu'il lut lentement
pres de la fenetre.

Il ne raconta jamais a personne ce que contenait ce mot, mais a partir
de ce jour il repara de nouveau des montres qui marchaient encore.
